blocks.text: Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: Eastern Hillsides is a hillside neighbourhood in southeast Chilliwack and a Neighbourhood Plan area, Schedule B4 of the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 2025, No. 5500). The plan was adopted in 2012, amended in 2017 to clarify development-approval requirements protecting future development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow, and updated a third time in 2025 as part of the OCP update.

Boundaries: west edge the Ryder Lake uplands, south edge Lookout Ridge and Elk Mountain, east edge the Cascade foothills / Fraser Valley Regional District boundary, and north edge the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1) and valley-floor farmland.
Internal roads named in City park listings include Allan Road, Rowanna Crescent and Marble Hill Road.
There are no condos or townhomes in this plan area. Homes are freehold detached houses on their own lots, built in development cells with set numbers of units under the neighbourhood plan.

Services are outside the plan area: the neighbourhood plan says there's no school inside it. The nearest recreation centre is Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way, Sardis), the nearest library is Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue), and Chilliwack General Hospital (45600 Menholm Road) and the urgent and primary care centre (#104–7955 Evans Road) are down on the valley floor.
Transit: no BC Transit route in the Chilliwack route overview runs into the Eastern Hillsides plan area; the overview lists routes 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 66, 71 and 72 for the city system.

Chilliwack OCP and the plan area: the current city-wide plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500; Eastern Hillsides is its Schedule B4 Neighbourhood Plan area. The 2050 OCP update replaced the plan's land-use designations with city-wide OCP designations, while the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area.

Zoning (Bylaw No. 5000): Suburban Hillside Residential (SHR) lots range from 360 m² to 990 m² depending on slope (minimum 12 m wide and 20 m deep); R3 Small Lot Residential is 360 m²; Hillside Residential (HR) is 0.2 ha with community water or 0.4 ha otherwise; and Rural Hillside (RH) is 8 ha. These detached-lot zones are why there are no apartments here. Check the zone for a specific property.

SSMUH — Chilliwack Bylaw 5395 (adopted June 18, 2024): brought the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing rules into Chilliwack's zoning. The Province granted Chilliwack an extension for part of the Proper neighbourhood and surrounding Hazel Park, with a new compliance date of December 31, 2030 — that extension area is not Eastern Hillsides, but it shows Chilliwack's SSMUH rollout is not uniform city-wide.

Hillside hazard rules — the defining rules for this area: steep slopes, main watercourses and ravines cross the plan area and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas; the 2017 amendments exist specifically to protect development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow, and Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. The City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands. Hillside lots are also subject to the 2050 OCP's Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5), under which a development permit is required for works including subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes.

The board boundary is a trap in this area. Chilliwack is CADREB territory, not FVREB — anyone quoting an "Eastern Hillsides median" from a SnapStats FVR report is quoting nothing, because that report has no Chilliwack section.

There is no school, recreation centre, library branch or bus route inside the plan area — the Neighbourhood Plan and the City/BC Transit listings say so directly. Every service trip goes to the valley floor or Sardis.

Marble Hill has a development moratorium history. Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported, and the City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands — check whether a lot sits in the moratorium area before counting on subdivision or a build.

The plan's unit counts still govern, even though its land-use labels changed. The 2050 OCP update replaced the Neighbourhood Plan's land-use designations with city-wide designations, but the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area.

The area's parks are the amenity. City listings include Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Crescent), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Road), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Road), Allan Creek Trail, Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Road) and the Elk Mountain Trail.

The historic wagon road is a protected heritage asset in the plan. The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) for protection, and states wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley.
Chilliwack's tax penalty is two-stepped in 2026: 5% on taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 4, 2026 — budget the full notice on either penalty date.

Where the townhomes are and what to know

items.t: Nearby areas: Ryder Lake to the west, Promontory and Sardis to the northwest across the valley floor, Rosedale / Bridal Falls toward the east along Highway 1, and Chilliwack Proper East at the northwest foot of the hillsides. Marble Hill is a named slope area inside the plan area. Search names buyers use: "Eastern Hillsides", "Eastern Hillsides Chilliwack", "Marble Hill Chilliwack".

There are no townhouses in this plan area. Homes are freehold detached houses on their own lots: early phases on large partly serviced lots, and small-lot zoning in later phases, built in development cells with set numbers of units.

Parks, recreation and health: parks and trails serving the area include Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Crescent), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Road), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Road), Allan Creek Trail, Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Road) and the Elk Mountain Trail. The nearest recreation centre is Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way, Sardis), the nearest library is Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue), and Chilliwack General Hospital (45600 Menholm Road) and the urgent and primary care centre (#104–7955 Evans Road) are on the valley floor.

Transit and roads: none of Chilliwack's BC Transit routes (51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 66, 71 and 72) run into the Eastern Hillsides plan area. Highway 1 forms the north edge, and the main roads inside include Allan Road, Rowanna Crescent and Marble Hill Road.

Eastern Hillsides homes are fee-simple detached houses: no strata, Form B or strata fees. Check the title, City zoning (Bylaw No. 5000), the OCP, and any registered covenants (including geotechnical covenants) or homeowners' association documents.
Flood / ALR: the plan area is hillside land above the valley floor, with valley-floor farmland along its north edge.

Heritage: the Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) as a heritage asset to protect, and states wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley — a title-and-permit check on lots touching those roads.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Eastern Hillsides

items.t: Lots are fee simple: the plan describes early phases as large partly serviced lots with houses, and small-lot zoning in later phases, built in development cells with set numbers of units. A lot here is your own title, with no strata corporation, fee or Form B; zoning, the OCP, hazard rules and any geotechnical covenants on title apply instead.

Lot character, only (Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 minimums — not measured sizes): SHR (Suburban Hillside Residential) minimum lot area is set by the bylaw's slope table and ranges from 360 m² to 990 m², minimum width 12 m, depth 20 m; R3 (Small Lot Residential) 360 m², width 12 m interior / 13.5 m corner; HR (Hillside Residential) 0.2 ha with a community water system and 0.4 ha in all other cases, width 25 m; RH (Rural Hillside) 8 ha, width 25 m. The zone and slope applying to any specific parcel: confirm per property.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: the plan's own words are "large semi-serviced lots" for the early development — servicing is not uniform hillside ground. The HR zone's minimum doubling (0.2 ha with a community water system, 0.4 ha otherwise) is the bylaw's own signal that community-water status changes what a lot can be. Whether a specific lot is on community water/sewer or on well/septic: confirm with the City and on title, parcel by parcel.
Land assemblies / development sites: The plan's development cells and unit allocations are plan regulation, not for-sale assemblies — never presented here as inventory.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the plan area is hillside land above the valley floor, with valley-floor farmland along its north edge. No ALR percentage for the plan area is published, so no split figure is stated.

The hazard character of the land itself: steep slopes, main watercourses and ravines cross the plan area and the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas; the City's Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable lands, and Council directed an expanded Marble Hill development moratorium area in 2017 after continuing ground movement was reported. Land value here cannot be read off lot size alone.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: There's no school inside the plan area; the neighbourhood plan says so directly. SD33 catchments are set by address with the district's School Locator. For example, 51314 Rowanna Crescent is in the catchment for East Chilliwack Elementary (49190 Chilliwack Central Road), Rosedale Traditional Community School (middle) and Chilliwack Secondary.

Parks and trails serving the area: Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Crescent), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Road), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Road), Allan Creek Trail, Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Road) and the Elk Mountain Trail. There's no recreation centre, library or bus route inside the plan area; the nearest recreation centre is Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way, Sardis), and the nearest library is Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue).

OCP: Chilliwack 2050, Bylaw No. 5500; Eastern Hillsides = Schedule B4: The 2050 update replaced the plan's land-use designations with city-wide OCP designations, while the plan's development cells and unit allocations continue to regulate how many units may be developed in the plan area. Under the previous OCP (Bylaw 2014, No. 4025) the Eastern Hillsides Comprehensive Development Plan formed part of the bylaw and Development Permit Area 2 covered the hillside/upland area — where older and newer documents differ, the 2050 OCP and the 2025-updated Neighbourhood Plan govern.

Slope is a price variable here, not a footnote. The same SHR zone carries a 360 m² minimum on gentle ground and a 990 m² minimum on steep ground — two lots with the same zone and the same area can have completely different subdivision value once the slope table and the 20%-slope development-permit trigger are applied.

The heritage on these lots is wagon roads. The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) as a heritage asset to protect, and states wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley — a title and site-history check on an older hillside parcel can surface alignments a buyer would not expect.
There is no bus, no school, no shop inside the plan area — by the sources, not by impression. A land buyer here is buying a drive-for-everything lot.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Eastern Hillsides

What sells in the Eastern Hillsides: individual fee-simple hillside lots, mostly large partly serviced lots with houses in the early phases, zoned SHR (minimum size depends on slope), HR (0.2 or 0.4 ha) or RH (8 ha). The key check here isn't ownership or services; it's the ground: steep slopes, identified hazard areas, and the Marble Hill slide and development moratorium area.

items.t: Fee-simple parcels are the acreage form: An Eastern Hillsides acreage purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — City zoning, the slope table, development-permit conditions and any geotechnical covenants on title govern.
Hobby vs working-farm ground: Whether a north-edge parcel carries farm use is a parcel-level check (ALR status, zoning, BC Assessment class).

Serviced vs unserviced ground: The HR zone minimum itself turns on servicing: 0.2 ha with a community water system, 0.4 ha in all other cases — so servicing is a lot-potential fact, not just a utility fact.

blocks.text: Where the acreages are and what to know

items.t: Plan history: the Eastern Hillsides Neighbourhood Plan was adopted by Council in 2012 as part of the OCP, amended in 2017 to clarify development-approval requirements protecting future development from rock fall, landslide or earthflow with unstable conditions, and updated a third time in 2025 as part of the OCP update.

Where acreage actually trades: on the plan area's large-lot cells — the plan describes early development as large semi-serviced lots with single-family homes, with small-lot zoning in later cells, organized into development cells with unit allocations. The acreage ground is the HR / RH hillside ground, not the SHR / R3 small-lot cells.

Parks and trails serving the area: Allan Creek Park (51314 Rowanna Crescent), Forest Gate Park (51442 Allan Road), Marble Hill Natural Area (7515 Marble Hill Road), Allan Creek Trail, Chilliwack Community Forest (51642 Allan Road) and the Elk Mountain Trail. There's no recreation centre or library inside the plan area; the nearest are Cheam Leisure Centre (45501 Market Way, Sardis) and Chilliwack Library (45860 First Avenue).

Hillside Development Permit Area: hillside lots are subject to the 2050 OCP's Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5), under which a development permit is required for works including subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes — slope measurement is a closing-condition item, not an afterthought. Heritage note in the same plan: the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) is identified as a heritage asset to protect; wagon roads in the area include Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley.

If you buy a strata home elsewhere, BC strata rules apply: check the Form B and depreciation report (required every 5 years for stratas with 5 or more lots), at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void, and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. None of this applies to a fee-simple Eastern Hillsides property.

Marble Hill is both a neighbourhood name and a slide area the City treats as undevelopable. The Greenspace Plan identifies the lower and upper Marble Hill slide areas as undevelopable land, and Council expanded a development moratorium there in 2017 after continued ground movement was reported. If a listing mentions Marble Hill, check the geotechnical reports and covenants, not just the view.

The wagon roads are a heritage layer on hillside title work: The Neighbourhood Plan identifies the historic wagon road (Browlee Road) as a heritage asset to protect, and names Nixon, Ruddock, Allan and Hinkley as wagon roads in the area — older hillside parcels can carry that history in their access and covenants.

Health care and daily services sit on the valley floor: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre, #104 – 7955 Evans Road (both Fraser Health), serve the city from below the hillsides — part of the real holding picture for acreage bought for its quiet.

faq.a: No. The listing checked describes a single-family house (5 bedrooms, 3,429 sq ft, built 2025) with sub-type "Strata" — a detached house, in a bare-land-style strata setting at most.
faq.q: A Marble Hill listing says "Strata" — is that a condo?

faq.a: The geotechnical check: the plan identifies geotechnical hazard areas, the 2017 amendments exist because of rock fall, landslide and earthflow risk, and the Marble Hill slide areas are identified as undevelopable — get the property's geotechnical reports and any covenants on title before pricing or removing subjects.
faq.q: What is the first check on any hillside lot here?

faq.a: Price it from the zone and the slope table: SHR minimum lot area alone swings from 360 m² to 990 m² depending on slope, HR doubles from 0.2 ha to 0.4 ha without a community water system, subdivision of land with 20% or greater slopes requires a development permit under the Hillside Development Permit Area, and the Marble Hill moratorium area requires extensive geotechnical evaluation first.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a hillside lot?

faq.a: There is no school inside the plan area at all. Run the exact address in the SD33 locator.
faq.q: Which schools serve an Eastern Hillsides address?

faq.a: The stock is detached hillside housing. Basis: above.
faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are there in Eastern Hillsides?

faq.a: No. The listing checked describes a single-family house with sub-type "Strata" — a detached house, in a bare-land-style strata setting at most.
faq.q: A Marble Hill listing says "Strata" — is that a townhouse?

faq.a: Outside this plan area — Chilliwack's townhouse stock is in Sardis, Garrison and the Vedder side of the city, under CADREB. Inside Eastern Hillsides, the realistic purchase is a fee-simple detached hillside house.
faq.q: If I want a townhouse near here, where do I look?

faq.a: An individual fee-simple hillside parcel — in the plan's early cells, a large semi-serviced lot with a single-family home — under SHR / HR / RH zoning inside the Schedule B4 Neighbourhood Plan area. There is no named acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product to buy instead.
faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" in Eastern Hillsides?

faq.a: By zone: HR minimum lot area is 0.2 ha with a community water system and 0.4 ha in all other cases; RH minimum is 8 ha; SHR runs 360 m² to 990 m² by the slope table. Those are creation minimums — the size of any listed parcel is its own survey.
faq.q: How big can an Eastern Hillsides acreage parcel be — and how small can a new lot be?

faq.a: If the land has slopes of 20% or greater, subdivision requires a development permit under the 2050 OCP Hillside Development Permit Area (Schedule D-5).
faq.q: Do I need a development permit to subdivide or build?

faq.a: There is no school inside the plan area, so every child travels. Run any other address in the SD33 locator.
